era: PlayStation 2 / Xbox / GameCube / PSP / Nintendo DS / Xbox 360 / PlayStation 3
summary: EA's street-football spin-off series; use Xbox for the sixth-generation full-console games and Xbox 360 for the HD-era entries, with handheld/mobile versions treated as alternates.

emulation.notes: Use Xbox route when compatible; PS2 is the reliable fallback.

primary.why: The first FIFA Street shipped on PS2, Xbox, and GameCube with the same core 4-on-4 street-football concept; Xbox is selected as the strongest sixth-generation console preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Xbox hardware or Xemu if compatible; use PCSX2 or Dolphin as fallback routes.

emulation.emulator: Xemu / PCSX2 fallback / PPSSPP for PSP comparison
emulation.notes: Use Xbox or PS2 for the full-console game.

primary.why: FIFA Street 2 shipped across PS2, Xbox, GameCube, PSP, Nintendo DS, and mobile phones; the Xbox version is the strongest full-console route, while the handheld versions are documented as worse at carrying the console innovations.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Xbox hardware or Xemu if compatible; use PSP/DS/mobile only for version comparison.

emulation.notes: Use original hardware where emulation compatibility is uncertain.

primary.why: FIFA Street 3 released on Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Nintendo DS; Xbox 360 is selected as the HD-console primary while DS is a separate handheld route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or a compatible preservation setup; use PS3 as an HD alternate.

entries.title: FIFA Street

emulation.notes: Use original hardware where emulation compatibility is uncertain.

primary.why: The 2012 FIFA Street reboot released on Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, uses the FIFA 12 engine, and includes national and club teams; Xbox 360 is selected as the primary HD preservation route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or a compatible preservation setup; use PS3 as an equivalent HD alternate if preferred.

entries.remaster_caveats: Reboot rather than a remaster of the EA Sports BIG trilogy.
